sentences.text: This tiny flying reptile possessed a wingspan measuring exactly 34.4 centimeters.
Scientists know the animal only from one nearly complete skeleton unearthed in the Tiaojishan Formation.
Lü Junchang and his team formally named the genus in 2012.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — shows large eye sockets and unconnected bones, indicating it was a late-stage juvenile.
Taxonomists classify it as a member of the rhamphorhynchid pterosaurs.
It inhabited the region of Mutoudeng in Qinglong County, Hebei Province, China.
This creature lived between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago during the Middle to Upper Jurassic.
Some researchers propose that Rhamphorhynchus may have evolved from Qinglongopterus because of their many shared traits.
Others argue that the similarity between the two genera suggests evolutionary stasis within rhamphorhynchine pterosaurs.
